column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
Describe a pond as an ecosystem: which of its parts are living and which are not, and why both count.
Sort a forest, a crop field, a lake and a fish tank in a room into those made by nature and those made by people.
Which living things can make their own food from sunlight and simple substances, and what name do we give them in an ecosystem?
Who depends on the producers for food, and in what different ways can they do so?
What would pile up in a forest, and what would the plants lack, if nothing broke down dead matter?
Grass is eaten by a goat, which is eaten by a human. What do we call this sequence, and what do we call each place in it?
Place a plant, a deer, a fox and a tiger on the correct trophic levels and say what each is called.
A deer eats a lot of grass but only a little of that becomes deer body. Where does the rest of the energy go?
If a level has 1000 units of energy, roughly how much can the next level receive, and what does that imply for how many levels can exist?
Can the energy a herbivore got from a plant ever be used by that plant again, and what happens to the amount of energy as you go up the levels?
A frog is eaten by snakes and by birds, and insects are eaten by frogs and by lizards. How would you draw all these feeding relationships?
In a typical ecosystem, which level has the most individuals and which the fewest?
A farmer sprays a field. By what routes can that chemical end up in the plants, fish and finally the people who eat them?
Why would a person at the top of a food chain carry more of a persistent chemical than a plant at the bottom?
Why would it be dangerous for life on the ground if the high-altitude ozone thinned out?
Which man-made chemicals were linked with the thinning of the ozone layer, and what international step was taken about them?
Why can a vegetable peel rot away in the soil while a plastic bottle stays for ages?
What has happened to the amount and kind of waste we produce as our life-style and packaging have changed, and what trouble does it cause?
